newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to lower, naphtha tightens.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to lower, naphtha tightens.

text.p: Med oil products were steady to lower on Tuesday but naphtha supplies tightened after Algeria's Skikda port closed due to bad weather.
Naphtha fell $1 to $222/$224 cif with traders offering a closer spread to fob prices, at $210/$212.
The Med looked balanced but slightly steadier after Skikda closed and several cargoes recently were sent to the U.S.
"With Skikda open I would call it balanced," a trader said. He said a 20,000 tonne paraffinic cargo was sold recently out of a Sicilian refinery at fob high quotes plus $7.
Gasoline edged lower with Italian demand satisfied.
A 30,000 tonne cargo of Eurograde and leaded traded recently at a $1-$1.50 premium to fob quotes in Italy.
An Italian trader said the market was "between balanced and a little long."
Gas oil slipped around $1.50 on weaker IPE futures. Heating oil premiums declined $1 to $2 on continuing abundant supply.

A cargo of Russian traded at cif high -$2.50 into east coast Greece on a very prompt basis, with one trader describing it as an almost distressed cargo. A cargo of Russian went at cif high +$1 basis Genoa for early delivery.

Buying interest in the eastern Med remained thin and a cargo of French grade heating oil, on the market for 10 days, remains offered out of Italy. But traders said they expected a tighter market in coming weeks with an estimated 10 cargoes of 0.2 heating oil due into Greece.
Fuel oil prices were steady, but traders continued to see bullish fundamentals going into winter.
Low sulphur fundamentals were reasonably tight after Italy's 250,000 tonne buying spree last week and dealers expected an arbitrage to open from the Caribbean to the Mediterranean in December.
